description: Delay overrides are stored as offsets of the base expansion delay (hotstrings.expansion_delay). Each vector starts from the shared default base (0.75 s), applies its steps through the driver's public API (effective seconds in, effective seconds out) and states what a reader must then resolve and what the override file must hold. Windows, macOS and Linux replay the same vectors.

vectors.description: A category delay set to 1.2 s over the 0.75 s base is stored as +0.45 s; moving the base to 1.0 s moves the delay to 1.45 s and leaves the file alone.
A section delay is its own offset; the category without a delay of its own waits the base.
0 means unlimited: it has its own flag and survives any base.
A -0.65 s offset on a 0.5 s base would be negative: the delay is clamped to one millisecond, never to 0.
Clearing a delay override leaves the category on the base, wherever it moved.
